properties.name: MEASURED across all 23 served skills: the ONE mechanic skill_lint enforces is at 23/23; every mechanic it does not enforce sits at 5-18/23. Presence tracks enforcement exactly — and the mechanics split into three kinds a factory treats differently
properties.statement:
MEASURED 2026-08-28 over `getting-started/skills/*/SKILL.md`, prompted by Anthony noticing that "we keep finding that a successful skill does something another does not" and wanting the good mechanic applied automatically rather than rediscovered.

═══ THE NUMBERS ═══

    graph-text-is-data rule    23/23   ← THE ONLY ONE skill_lint ENFORCES
    says what it CANNOT do     18/23
    honest limits section       8/23
    loop_status before finish   8/23
    an anti-pattern list        7/23
    names what it is NOT        5/23
    a MEASURED example          5/23

⭐⭐ **PRESENCE TRACKS ENFORCEMENT EXACTLY.** The single checked mechanic is universal. Every unchecked one is between a fifth and four-fifths, and which skills have it is a matter of what its author happened to write that day. This is not a claim about diligence; it is what an unenforced convention looks like at n=23.

═══ ⭐ AND IT ANSWERS THE NODE'S OWN TEST, IN THE SKILL DOMAIN ═══

That node poses the cheapest honest test as: *"name a change that WOULD have required editing all 173 tools. If one exists, the factory earns itself."* Posed for tools, it was unanswered. **For skills it is answered now: "every skill states its honest limits" requires editing 15 of 23.** A class change needing N edits exists today, and there are at least four more in the table above.

═══ 🛑 BUT THE MECHANICS ARE NOT ONE KIND, AND THAT IS THE REFINEMENT ═══

The node's counterweight 1 stands — *"a factory guarantees the mechanics are PRESENT, never that they are RIGHT"* — and the measurement shows it applies to some mechanics and not others:

**① BOILERPLATE, where presence IS correctness.** The graph-text-is-data line; having a slash command. One right answer, no judgement, and a linter cannot be satisfied dishonestly. **A factory owns this class completely, and the 23/23 proves it works.**

**② JUDGEMENT, where presence is NOT correctness.** "Honest limits", "a measured example", "what it cannot do". Forcing these into 15 skills yields 15 sections written to satisfy a linter — exactly the `internal`-by-default trap the node already names, manufactured at scale. **A factory can require the SECTION and cannot supply the HONESTY.** What it can do is make the omission visible and attributable rather than invisible.

**③ TOOL-SIDE, which cannot be fixed by editing skills at all.** The mechanic measured to actually work today is not in any SKILL.md: the `Artifact` tool's own description says the agent MUST load `artifact-design` before writing the file. Of five skills used in a long session, three were invoked because the user typed a command, one because a tool demanded it, and one was genuinely self-invoked — see `fact:the-author-of-a-skill-did-not-use-it-an-hour-later`. **No reflow2 tool makes any reflow2 skill a precondition of itself.** That is a class change across the tool surface, not the skill surface, and no amount of editing SKILL.md files reaches it.

⚠️ **SO THE FACTORY QUESTION SPLITS.** For ① it is cheap and demonstrably effective. For ② it risks manufacturing the ambiguity the node warns about. For ③ it is aimed at the wrong artifact entirely — and ③ is the one with evidence of changing an agent's behaviour.

⚠️ WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH: the seven mechanics were chosen by the measuring agent and detected by regex over prose, so both the list and the counts are approximate — a skill may honour a mechanic in words the pattern missed. The claim that presence tracks enforcement rests on ONE enforced mechanic; a second enforced one would test it properly. And nothing here says which mechanics are WORTH having, only which are unevenly present.
